case_analysis.thread_summary: The thread covers planning and pre-test preparation for Bluetooth qualification of an automotive head unit / commercial model. The team works through quotation updates, profile test scope, ICS preparation, PTS equipment, sample setup, and Qualification Workspace handling. HOGP is removed from the test scope after confirming it is not implemented, reducing the profile-test estimate. The consultant also reviews ICS consistency and profile-test readiness issues before testing proceeds.
case_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The main qualification issue is how to combine existing referenced designs without creating avoidable ICS modification obligations. The consultant explains that overlapping Controller-related references should not both be included, and that inter-layer dependency inconsistencies should be handled through the applicable ICS Form Inconsistencies / TCW route rather than by modifying referenced Core-layer ICS. Profile qualification requires PTS evidence for supported profiles, and only implemented profiles should remain in scope. The thread also covers practical PTS constraints: profiles not advertised in SDP may be untestable without test software, v4.2 PTS dongles cannot cover newer LE modes such as AoA/AoD, LE Audio, or Channel Sounding, and RF/RF PHY testing needs a test-mode-capable DUT.
case_analysis.key_decision_logic: The consultant's core logic is to preserve valid reuse of referenced designs while avoiding unnecessary modification of referenced ICS layers, because post-July-2024 rules can trigger full test-report requirements for modified layers. Profile test scope must match actual implementation and ICS support, not the initial estimate or assumed feature list. Testing readiness is determined by whether the DUT can expose each target profile to PTS and enter the required RF/RF PHY test modes. Manual confirmation during PTS tests is acceptable where PTS relies on operator judgment and the applicant has already confirmed real-device behavior.
case_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Including an unimplemented profile such as HOGP could add unnecessary profile testing and an unnecessary ￥100,000 profile-test item. Incorrectly modifying referenced Core-layer ICS could trigger avoidable full-layer test-report obligations. Poor ICS preparation can cause consistency-check rework or failed PTS execution, especially where mandatory items are missing or unsupported items are marked supported. If the DUT cannot advertise or expose profiles such as AVRCP independently, PTS testing may require test firmware or other preparation, causing delay.
case_analysis.consulting_takeaway: Before quotation and testing, lock the actual implemented profile scope, verify ICS mandatory/support selections, confirm referenced-design combinations in Workspace, and check that the DUT can expose each profile and enter required test modes. Avoid fixing inter-layer dependency inconsistencies by modifying referenced ICS unless the resulting test obligations are understood.
